subject.title: fix(grep): bound file reads with size cap in default grep operations

question: Should default grep silently omit context for existing regular files above a fixed 50 MiB limit in exchange for preventing unbounded memory reads?
rationale: The branch fixes a real resource-risk path, but it deliberately replaces existing large-file context behavior with degradation and introduces a hard-coded product limit rather than a purely internal correction.

options.title: Accept the 50 MiB default cap
options.body: Land the cap after current-head real behavior proof confirms the resulting grep output is understandable and the compatibility tradeoff is intentional.

options.title: Use a different product contract
options.body: Adjust the bounded-read behavior or result presentation so users receive an explicit, supported indication when matching context is omitted.

options.title: Defer the behavior change
options.body: Keep the current implementation unmerged until maintainers choose a broader grep large-file policy.

recommendation.title: Accept the 50 MiB default cap
recommendation.body: Land the cap after current-head real behavior proof confirms the resulting grep output is understandable and the compatibility tradeoff is intentional.
